comment: Ground-truth oracle for the incident_response extraction eval (PR-2). This is what a TRUSTWORTHY extractor should produce from slack_messages.json + notion_runbook.json. Rules encoded here, to be asserted by the PR-2 eval harness: (1) every evidence.quote is a verbatim substring of the referenced source's text — the evidence-integrity gate; (2) valid_time.from is set ONLY when a date is stated in the evidence, else null/unknown — the model must never invent a start; (3) status tiers reflect corroboration: 'observed' needs >=2 INDEPENDENT sources (distinct authors, or doc+person), single-source stays 'candidate'; (4) contradictory answers to the same claim_key coexist as 'disputed' with distinct fingerprints — the doc never silently wins; (5) chatter is refused, not attested. No field here is a confidence score: confidence is computed by the system, not labeled here.

attestations.claim: P0 incidents open a war room in #incidents

evidence.author: priya
evidence.quote: Opening the war room in #incidents now

evidence.author: dan
evidence.quote: war room open in #incidents for the P0

attestations.notes: Two independent authors (priya, dan) -> observed. No start date stated -> valid_from stays null.

attestations.claim: Incident comms and escalation happen in #incidents

evidence.author: sarah
evidence.quote: since March we run all incident comms out of #incidents, not #engineering

attestations.notes: Observed practice with an EXPLICIT stated start ('since March') -> valid_from = 2026-03, basis stated. Conflicts with the documented #engineering answer -> disputed. This is also the divergence/timeline signal for PR-4.

evidence.author: notion:runbook
evidence.quote: All production incidents are escalated in #engineering

attestations.notes: Documented baseline + a pre-March message. Shares claim_key with the #incidents answer but a DISTINCT fingerprint, so both coexist active as a dispute. m4 implies this ended ~2026-03 (a close/correction candidate PR-2 may act on); the doc must NOT silently win.

attestations.claim: On-call engineer must acknowledge a PagerDuty page within 5 minutes or it escalates to the team lead

evidence.author: dan
evidence.quote: on-call ack within 5 min is the rule, PagerDuty escalates to the team lead if not

attestations.notes: Both evidence chunks are authored by dan -> only ONE independent source -> stays 'candidate', not 'observed'. Tests the independence rule (a re-quote by the same author is not corroboration).

attestations.claim: The incident commander is the engineering manager on call

evidence.author: priya
evidence.quote: I'll run point as incident commander — I'm the eng manager on call this week

attestations.notes: Single source -> candidate. Uncertainty is shown, not smoothed into a confident fact.

attestations.claim: A postmortem is required for P0 and P1 incidents and is filed in Notion

evidence.author: notion:runbook
evidence.quote: A postmortem is required for all P0 and P1 incidents and must be filed in Notion

evidence.author: priya
evidence.quote: I'll write the postmortem in Notion — required for anything P0 or P1

attestations.notes: Doc AND observed behavior agree -> corroborated/observed. Contrast with the escalation divergence: agreement strengthens, disagreement disputes.

refusals.notes: Sentiment about the process, not a statement of how the org operates. Only attestable as 'X expressed Y', never as fact.
A question/proposal ('should we...? maybe worth trying'), not adopted practice. Intent != state.
Joke. No operational claim to ground.

divergences.notes: Bonus oracle for PR-4. The doc (last edited 2025-11) is stale; observed practice moved to #incidents in March 2026. Only reconstructable because the ledger keeps both, dated.
